title: The cycle (Judges 2:16–19)
hookLine: forget, suffer, cry out, be rescued, forget again: the book of Judges in one loop

cards: Be rescued. Forget again. That's the book of Judges in one loop, and the book lays it out itself, before any of its well-known stories begin.

Joshua has died, and his whole generation with him. Then the text says it plainly: "there arose another generation after them, which knew not the LORD, nor yet the works which he had done for Israel."
The people who carried stones up out of the river are gone. The next generation, it seems, never heard the answer to the question the stones were built to raise.

teach.b: Today's word is judge. In English it sounds like a courtroom: a robe, a gavel.
Listen to how the book introduces them, in the King James Bible: "Nevertheless the LORD raised up judges, which delivered them out of the hand of those that spoiled them." Delivered.
These judges are rescuers first, leaders raised up in a crisis. Some lead in battle. Some settle disputes.
The Hebrew word is shofet. Now the loop. The people turn to other gods.
They're handed over to raiders. They groan under it, and here the text says something tender: "it repented the LORD because of their groanings by reason of them that oppressed them and vexed them."

teach.h: GOD IS MOVED BY THE GROANING.
teach.b: God is moved by their groaning. A judge is raised up, and while that judge lives, there's rest. Then verse nineteen: "when the judge was dead, that they returned, and corrupted themselves more than their fathers."
More than their fathers. It isn't a circle.

teach.h: NOT A CIRCLE, A SPIRAL DOWN.
teach.b: It's a spiral, heading down. By the book's last verse, the narrator puts it in one line: "In those days there was no king in Israel: every man did that which was right in his own eyes."
Readers find two things in this loop at once.

One is a warning: the first step is forgetting, and forgetting makes no noise. In chapter two, a generation grows up without the story first, and only then do the other gods follow. The other is mercy.
Again and again, when they cry out, someone is sent. What runs short is remembering.

how: Some Christians read Judges 2 as the key to the whole book, and some preachers use its cycle to speak about patterns of forgetting God and returning.

the cycle in Judges returns to the same place each time

games.q: you're living in the days of the judges. a judge has rescued your people, and now that judge has died. what does the text say happens next?
o: they go back to the old ways, worse than before.
they choose a king right away.
games.why: "when the judge was dead... they returned, and corrupted themselves more than their fathers." the loop starts again, lower down.

practice: Let one quiet loop in your life come to mind: the same argument, the same late-night scrolling, the same Monday promise gone by Thursday.
Trace it once, slowly: where it starts, the moment you stop paying attention, the groaning, what rescues you for a while, and see it whole without beating yourself up.
If you pray, name it to God, the way Israel groaned; if you don't, simply hold it in view.

wordCard.voice: Judge. In the book of Judges, a shofet: someone raised up in a crisis to deliver and set things right. Not a robe and a gavel.

orig.note: Hebrew: judge. Judges 2:16 says the LORD raised up shoftim, judges, which delivered them.

carryVoice: Your line: break the cycle. The loop starts where the forgetting starts. Day seven hundred two, done.
